I am estimating FED effort for a ticket (SFCC-173) that wants "FAQ and Article structured data schema (JSON-LD) authored via Contentful". I need to know exactly what the Contentful content model and front-end integration looks like TODAY. Be very thorough, cite absolute file paths.

Investigate and report:

1. **Content model source of truth.** List every file in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`. For EACH content type, give the content type id, name, and its fields (name, type, required, localized). I specifically need to know: does an **FAQ** content type exist? Does an **Article** / blog / editorial content type exist? Does anything have SEO metadata fields (metaTitle, metaDescription, seo, structuredData, jsonLd)? Quote field definitions where relevant.

2. **Template build/install pipeline.** Read `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` and `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` at a high level. What is the workflow to add a NEW content type — what files change, what command installs it, and what is the per-environment story (how many Contentful environments)? Check `package.json` scripts for `sync:contentful` / `install:contentful` / `config:contentful`.

3. **Front-end Contentful integration.** List and describe everything under `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. Read `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`. How is content fetched — GraphQL or CDA REST? Client-side or SSR? Is there a hook (grep for `useContentful`, `contentfulClient`, `createClient`)? Find where Contentful data enters the page — grep `contentful` across `overrides/app/pages/`.
   - Is it Contentful **Studio Experiences** (experience builder)? Check `overrides/app/pages/experience/`, `overrides/app/components/contentful/experienceBySlug/`, and grep for `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in package.json.

4. **Localisation.** How does the Contentful integration handle 11 locales / 8 sites? Is a locale passed to the Contentful query? Grep for `locale` inside `overrides/app/components/contentful/` and the contentful config. Are content types marked `localized: true`?

5. **Docs.** Read any Contentful integration doc in `.docs/integration/` (look for a file matching `*contentful*`). Also grep `.docs/` for "FAQ", "Article", "structured data", "JSON-LD", "schema" and report anything relevant with the file path.

6. **Rendering of rich text.** Is there a rich-text renderer (grep `@contentful/rich-text-react-renderer`, `richText`)? Relevant because an FAQ answer body would be rich text and JSON-LD needs plain text.

Return a structured findings report. Do not write any files. Be explicit about what does NOT exist.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

content.content:
# 02 — Contentful (CMS)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

In scope:

- Reading published content via the Delivery API
- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
- Live preview in Contentful Studio
- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries

Out of scope of this document:

- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |

═══ scripts/contentful/README.md ═══
# Contentful tooling

Zimmermann uses **two different Contentful surfaces**. Keep them straight — they live in different places and are managed by different tools.

## 1. Content types (editorial schemas)

**What:** Schemas for editorial entries authors fill in (e.g. `footerConfig`, `link`).
**Where:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — plain JS, one file per content type. This is the **sole** source of truth for a content type's fields, including `required`/`localized`/`validations` — there is no separate migration file layered on top.
**How:** Pushed as one organization-scoped **Environment Template**, then installed into each environment. This is Contentful's current recommended mechanism — content models are authored once at the organization level, not created independently per space/environment (see the `contentful-management` SDK's `client.environmentTemplate.*` API).

```bash
npm run sync:contentful                                   # build/update the template from content-types/*.js
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev                # push it into one environment
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev --dry-run       # validate only, no changes
```

Driven by [buildTemplate.js](./buildTemplate.js) (assembles `content-types/*.js` into one
`EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`) and
[setup/installTemplate.mjs](./setup/installTemplate.mjs) (validates then installs the
template's current version into `--target <environmentId>`, polling until the install
reaches a terminal status). Reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`,
and `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` from `.env`.

Promotion order: `dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master` — run `install:contentful`
against each target in turn. Contentful tracks each environment's install status/version
natively (`environmentTemplateInstallation`) — there's no hand-rolled migration-history
content type and no separate drift-detection script, since every environment installs
from the same versioned template and can't drift from it the way independently-synced
environments used to.

**Entries are a separate concern from the template.** Environment Templates cover
content-*type* schema only — seed data (e.g. the canonical `region` entries) needs its
own per-environment script, run after that environment has the relevant content type
installed:

```bash
npm run seed:contentful-regions -- --target dev
```

See [setup/seedRegions.mjs](./setup/seedRegions.mjs).

To add a new content type: drop a new file in [content-types/](./content-types/) following
the shape of [footerConfig.js](./content-types/footerConfig.js) (explicit `localized`
per field), then re-run `sync:contentful` followed by `install:contentful` per environment.

## 2. Studio Experiences component definitions (visual builder)

**What:** Registers Zimmermann React components with Contentful Studio Experiences so authors can drop them onto pages in the visual builder.
**Where:** `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — one `.tsx` per component, plus a single generated `definitions.ts` registry.
**How:** Imported at runtime by `defineComponents` — no push step. The registry is **generated from code**; never edit `definitions.ts` by hand.

### Author workflow

1. Create or update your component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`.
2. Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before the component's `const` declaration.
3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type with a `@cf` JSDoc tag:

   ```tsx
   type MyComponentProps = {
     /** @cf Headline */
     headline: string;

     /** @cf Hero Image, media */
     heroImage?: string;

     /** @cf skip */
     internalId?: string;
   };
   ```

4. Run the generator:

   ```bash
   npm run generate:contentful
   ```

   This rewrites `definitions.ts` automatically. Commit both the annotated component and the updated `definitions.ts`.

5. The pre-commit hook runs the generator automatically when an `experiences/*.tsx` file is staged, keeping `definitions.ts` in sync.

For full tag syntax and control options, see the `/contentful-register-component` skill.

### CI check

```bash
npm run generate:contentful:check
```

Exits zero if `definitions.ts` is up to date, non-zero (with a diff) if regeneration is needed. Wire into CI to catch a forgotten regenerate.

## Don't cross the streams

- A Studio Experiences component (`experiences/*.tsx`) does **not** belong in [content-types/](./content-types/) — `buildTemplate.js` does not understand it.
- A content-type definition (`content-types/*.js`) does **not** belong in `experiences/` — it is an API artefact, not a runtime component.
- **Never edit `definitions.ts` directly.** The file is autogenerated; manual edits will be overwritten on the next run.

## 2. Template build/install pipeline

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`**
Reads every `.js` in `content-types/` (`fs.readdirSync().filter(f => f.endsWith('.js')).sort()`), maps each to a `contentTypeTemplate` + optional `editorInterfaceTemplate`, then get-or-creates the org-scoped template by **name** under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` and bumps its version. Touches no space or environment. Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` + `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`.

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs`**
Validates then installs the template's current version into `--target <envId>`, polling `environmentTemplateInstallation` until terminal status (120s timeout). Refuses to install on any unresolved validation finding unless `--force`. Supports `--dry-run`, `--takeover <ids>` (adopt pre-existing unmanaged content types), `--delete-deleted-fields`.

### Workflow to add a NEW content type

Per `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/README.md`:

1. Drop a new file in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` following `footerConfig.js`'s shape (explicit `localized` per field — no migration layer on top).
2. `npm run sync:contentful` — builds/updates the org template.
3. `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` — **once per environment**.

**Files that change for SFCC-173:** one new `scripts/contentful/content-types/faq.js` (+ likely `faqItem.js`), and optionally `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`) and `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` (TS types).

`TARGET_ENVIRONMENTS = ['dev','test','sit','staging','uat']` plus `master`. Promotion order is **`dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master`** (prod via the `production` alias). `install:contentful` must be run **6 times**, one per target. There is no batch/all-envs flag.

## 3. Front-end Contentful integration

### `overrides/app/components/contentful/` — only 3 files, all Studio Experiences

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts` — **empty file (0 bytes).**
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/contentful/experienceBySlug/index.tsx` — the main Studio Experiences renderer.
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` — **12 lines, currently `defineComponents([])`.** Autogenerated; header comment says every `experiences/*.tsx` component was removed as unused Hardi-era scaffolding. **No Zimmermann component is registered with Studio Experiences today.**

### Two parallel, unconnected integration paths

**Path A — Studio Experiences (experience builder): YES, it is in use.**
- `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` `^3.8.8` and `@contentful/live-preview` `^4.10.1` are direct dependencies (`package.json` lines 129–131).
- One Experience Type covers the whole site: `const EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID = 'zimmermann'` in `experienceBySlug/index.tsx`. Every page is an entry distinguished by `slug`.
- Entry points: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx` (`/:slug`), `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (`/`, slug `homepage`), `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx` (`/preview`), and `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/categoryPath/index.tsx` (renders `<Experience slug={segments[0]} />` for single-segment unmatched paths).
- Fetching via `useFetchBySlug` / `useFetchById` — **client-side hooks**.

**Path B — hand-rolled CDA REST, for discrete content types.**
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — exports `useContentfulEntry<T>(entryId, preview, locale)` and `useContentfulEntries<T>(contentType, preview, locale, filter, enabled, include)`. Raw `fetch()` inside `useEffect`, with `AbortController`, plus a hand-written `resolveLinkedAssets()` that walks `includes.Asset` / `includes.Entry` with cycle detection.
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts` — memoised official `createClient()` from `contentful`, centralising the CPA-token gate. **Used only by the Experiences pages**, not by Path B.
- Consumers of Path B: `useUiCopy.ts`, `useHeaderNav.ts`, `useSizeGuide.ts`, `components/footer/index.tsx`, `components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx`, `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmBenefits/index.tsx`.

### GraphQL or REST?

**REST CDA only. There is no GraphQL client, no `gql` template tag, no `.graphql` file anywhere in `overrides/`.** URLs are hand-built in `useContentful.ts`:

```ts
`${baseUrl}/spaces/${spaceId}/environments/${environment}/entries?${query}&access_token=${token}&include=${include}${localeParam}`
```

**This contradicts the doc.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3 claims *"GraphQL for composed pages — where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API"* and §6 claims *"GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses"*. Neither is true in code.

### Client-side or SSR?

**100% client-side.** `grep -rn "getProps" overrides/app/pages/*/index.tsx` returns **nothing** — no page implements SSR data fetching. Both paths fetch in `useEffect` after hydration.
